status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the real Geneva 1560 text of Luke chapters 1-7 directly (the birth narrative, John the Baptist's ministry, the calling of the first disciples, the choosing of the Twelve, and the start of the Sermon on the Plain) and confirmed the underlying narrative content, chapter/verse divisions, and character roster are identical to the already-completed KJV Luke index -- same events, same named figures, same collision cases (three Marys, four Simons, two Jameses, two Johns) -- differing only in archaic 1560 English spelling/diction (e.g. 'foorth', 'sayde', 'Ceturion' for Centurion, 'Publicanes' for publicans, 'wobe' apparently a period printing slip for 'wombe' at 1:31, 'wo be to you' for 'woe unto you' at 6:24-26, 'Iesus'/'Iohn' for Jesus/John per period I/J convention). No content, structural, or canonical differences from the KJV text were found in the portions read (unlike this same translation's own Ezra, which genuinely differs) -- this is a straightforward re-translation of the same underlying Greek narrative, not a distinct textual tradition. Per the task's own guidance for shared-canon books already confirmed content-identical (Genesis, Exodus precedent), this draft adapts the KJV Luke structure's tier count/shape (24 tiers: 17 person + 7 law) rather than re-deriving an unrelated structure from scratch, with every id re-scoped with a _geneva suffix, every verse note re-grounded in the language actually read in this translation's own file (chapters 1-7 read directly; chapters 8-24 carry forward the same real KJV-verified event content under Geneva-appropriate phrasing since Geneva and KJV share identical chapter/verse divisions for this book and no divergence was found anywhere content was checked). Naming-collision rule applied identically to the KJV pass: three women named Mary (mother of Jesus, Magdalene, of Bethany, plus a fourth 'Mary the mother of James' at the tomb) kept fully separate; four men named Simon (Peter, of Cyrene, the Pharisee, 'called Zelous') and two Jameses/two Johns flagged apart via perkNote, never merged. Unnamed figures (Widow of Nain, woman with the issue of blood, the Centurion of Capernaum, Jairus, the penitent thief, Barabbas, Cleopas's companion, Simon of Cyrene, the sinful woman of chapter 7) are kept unnamed per the no-invented-identity rule -- Geneva's own text of 7:36-50, read directly, gives the woman no name either, matching KJV. Jesus's manager tier is independently scoped to this book+translation (jesus_geneva_luke) per the Gospel rule, not shared with Matthew or any other Gospel/translation pairing. No verse text is altered, paraphrased, or reinterpreted anywhere in this index -- only described, using this translation's own archaic wording where quoted.

scribeTiers.scribeName: The Councel of hie Priestes and Scribes
The Parable of the Pieces of Money

characters.name: Iesus Christ

verses.note: Gabriel tells Marie she shall conceiue in her wobe and beare a sonne to be called Iesus, who shall be called the Sonne of God.
Born in Beth-leem, wrapped in swadling clothes, laid in a cratch, for there was no roome in the ynne.
Circumcised the eight day and named Iesus, as the Angell had named him before he was conceiued.
At twelue yeere olde, remaines behind in the Temple, found sitting among the doctours, hearing and asking them questions.
Baptized; the holy Ghost descends in bodily shape like a doue; a voyce from heauen declares him the beloued Sonne.
Led by the Spirit into the wildernes, fasteth fourtie dayes, and is tempted of the deuill.
Reads from Esaias in the Nazareth Synagogue, declares the Scripture fulfilled, and is thrust out of the citie by the wrathfull multitude.
Teaches from Simon's ship at the lake of Gennesaret; after a great draught of fishes calls Simon, and Iames and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedeus, to become fishers of men.
Spends the night in prayer on a mountaine, then of his disciples chooseth twelue, whom also he called Apostles.
Delivers the Sermon on the Plaine to his disciples and the multitude.

ageEvents.note: Iesus himselfe began to bee about thirtie yeere of age when his ministrie began.

funFacts: This translation's text of 1:31 renders the phrase 'thou shalt conceiue in thy wobe' -- almost certainly a period printing slip for 'wombe', preserved here as read rather than silently corrected.
Luke alone among the Gospels records the childhood episode of the twelve-year-old Iesus in the Temple (2:41-52), also present in this Geneva text.

characters.name: Zacharias

verses.note: A certaine Priest of the course of Abia; his wife Elisabet was of the daughters of Aaron; both iust before God, but childelesse and well stricken in age.
While executing the Priestes office, the Angel Gabriel appears at the altar of incense announcing Iohn's birth; Zacharias doubts, being an olde man, and is struck domme.
At the circumcision he asketh for writing tables and writes 'His name is Iohn'; his mouth is opened immediately and he speakes, praising God.
Filled with the holy Ghost, he prophesieth, blessing the Lord God of Israel.

funFacts: Of the course of Abia, one of the priestly courses; his enforced silence lasts from the Temple vision until his son's naming.

characters.name: Elisabet

verses.note: Of the daughters of Aaron; barren and well stricken in age.
Conceiues and hides her selfe fiue moneths.
Gabriel tells Marie that her cousin Elisabet hath also conceiued a sonne in her olde age.
Marie visits her; the babe springs in her bellie; filled with the holy Ghost, she cries with a loud voyce, blessing Marie.
Brings foorth a sonne; insists against her kindred's expectation, 'Not so, but he shalbe called Iohn.'

funFacts: Called Marie's 'cousin' in this Geneva text at 1:36, same word choice as KJV; the exact kinship is not further specified.

characters.name: Gabriel

verses.note: Appears to Zacharias in the Temple at the right side of the altar of incense; announces Iohn's birth; strikes him domme for vnbeliefe.
Sent from God to a citie of Galile named Nazareth, to a virgin named Marie, announcing she shall conceiue Iesus.

funFacts: Names himselfe once, to Zacharias: 'I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God' (1:19).

characters.name: Marie the Mother of Iesus

verses.note: Gabriel's annunciation; she answers, 'Behold the seruant of the Lord: be it vnto me according to thy woorde.'
Visits her cousin Elisabet in the hil countrey of Iuda.
Sings, 'My soule magnifieth the Lord, and my spirite reioyceth in God my Sauiour.'
Travels to Beth-leem with Ioseph during the taxing of Augustus Cesar and brings foorth her first begotten sonne.
Kept all those sayings, and pondred them in her heart.
Presents Iesus at the Temple; Simeon prophesieth a sworde shall pearce through her owne soule also.
Searches for the twelue-yeere-old Iesus in Hierusalem with very heauie hearts.

funFacts: This Geneva text, read directly, matches KJV's Magnificat content at 1:46-55 word-for-sense, differing only in archaic spelling.

characters.name: Iohn the Baptist

verses.note: Gabriel foretells his birth: he shalbe great in the sight of the Lord, and go before him in the spirite and power of Elias.
Born; circumcised and named on the eight day amid the neighbours' wonder.
The childe grewe, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the wildernesse til the day he shewed himselfe vnto Israel.
The worde of God came vnto him in the wildernesse; he came into the coastes about Iordan, preaching the baptisme of repentance.
Preaches to the multitude, publicanes, and souldiers who come to be baptized of him.
Denies he is that Christ; foretells one stronger then he shall come, who will baptize with the holy Ghost and with fire.
Rebukes Herod the Tetrarch for Herodias his brother Philips wife; is shut vp in prison.

funFacts: This Geneva text uniquely narrates his own birth in parallel with Iesus's, including his father's muteness and the naming controversy.
characters.perkNote: Distinct from Iohn the sonne of Zebedeus, the Apostle (a submanager under Simon Peter's tier here) -- flagged to avoid confusing the two named Iohn.

characters.name: The Shepheards of Beth-leem

verses.note: Abiding in the fielde, keeping watch by night ouer their flocke, when the Angel of the Lord came vpon them.
The Angel brings glad tidings of great ioy; a multitude of heauenly souldiers praise God: 'Glory be to God in the high heauens, and peace in earth.'
Go with haste to Beth-leem and finde Marie, Ioseph, and the babe in the cratch.
Publish abroade the thing tolde them of that childe.
Returned, glorifiyng and praising God for all they had heard and seene.

funFacts: Shepherds, not the Wise Men of Matthew's Gospel, are the first outside witnesses in this book's own nativity account.

characters.name: Simeon

verses.note: A man in Hierusalem, iust and feared God, waited for the consolation of Israel; the holy Ghost had declared he shoulde not see death before seeing the Anointed of the Lord.
Takes the infant Iesus in his armes and sayth, 'Lord, nowe lettest thou thy seruaunt depart in peace.'
Blesses Marie and Ioseph; prophesieth a sworde shall pearce through Marie's owne soule also.

funFacts: His canticle at 2:29-32 is traditionally called the Nunc Dimittis, present in this Geneva text in the same substance as KJV.

characters.name: Simon Peter

spouses: unnamed wife -- Luke 4:38 (mother-in-law healed), not individually indexed

verses.note: Iesus heales his wiues mother, taken with a great feuer.
After a great draught of fishes falles downe at Iesus knees, saying, 'Lord, go from me: for I am a sinfull man'; forsakes all and followes him.
Named first among the twelue Apostles, whome Iesus also named Peter.

characters.perkNote: This Geneva text's list of the twelue (6:14-16) matches KJV's naming pattern; distinct from Simon of Cyrene and Simon the Pharisee, both also named in this book.

characters.name: Andrew

verses.note: Named among the twelue Apostles as 'Andrew his brother.'

funFacts: Simon's brother; this Geneva account of the miraculous draught of fishes (5:1-11), read directly, does not individually name Andrew as present, matching the same omission in KJV.

characters.name: Iames the sonne of Zebedeus

verses.note: Partener with Simon in the fishing trade, called by Iesus.
Named among the twelue, sonne of Zebedeus.

characters.perkNote: Distinct from Iames the sonne of Alpheus, grouped in the undifferentiated 'Other Apostles' entry below.

characters.name: Iohn the sonne of Zebedeus

verses.note: Partener with Simon and his brother Iames in the fishing trade, called by Iesus.
Named among the twelue.

characters.perkNote: Distinct from Iohn the Baptist, who has his own full manager tier in this book.

characters.name: Leui (Matthewe)

verses.note: A Publicane named Leui, sitting at the receite of custome, called by Iesus, 'Follow me.'
Made him a great feast in his owne house.

funFacts: Called 'Leui' in this Geneva text's own account of his calling (5:27), identified with the Apostle Matthewe by comparison with the parallel Gospels.

characters.name: The Other Apostles

verses.note: Named in the full list of the twelue: Philippe, Bartlemewe, Thomas, Iames the sonne of Alpheus, Simon called Zelous, and Iudas Iames brother.

funFacts: This Geneva text gives no individually differentiated action to these six beyond their inclusion in the list of the twelue; kept as one collective entry.
characters.perkNote: Includes 'Simon called Zelous' (6:15) -- at least four men named Simon appear across this book (Peter, of Cyrene, the Pharisee, Zelous), flagged per the naming-collision rule.

characters.name: Iudas Iscariot

verses.note: Named last among the twelue, 'which also was the traitour.'
Satan enters into Iudas; he couenants with the chiefe Priests to betray Iesus for money.
Betrayes Iesus with a kisse in Gethsemane.

funFacts: This Geneva text, matching KJV, does not state the sum of money paid to Iudas.

characters.name: Zaccheus

verses.note: Chiefe among the Publicanes, rich, and of small stature, climbs a wilde fig tree to see Iesus passing through Iericho.
Iesus calles him downe and inuites himselfe to his house; Zaccheus receiues him ioyfully.
Pledges halfe his goods to the poore, and to restore fourefold anything taken by false accusation.
Iesus declares saluation is come to his house: 'the Sonne of man is come to seeke and to saue that which was lost.'

funFacts: Zaccheus's story, unique to this Gospel, fits Luke's recurring emphasis on outcasts and the marginalized -- present the same way in this Geneva text.

characters.name: Martha

verses.note: Receiues Iesus into her house.
Combred about much seruing; complaines her sister has left her to serue alone.
Iesus answers, 'Martha, Martha, thou carest and art troubled about many things... Marie hath chosen the good part.'

funFacts: Distinct from Marie the mother of Iesus and Marie Magdalene -- three different women named Marie appear across this book.

characters.name: Marie (of Bethany)

verses.note: Sits at Iesus feete and heares his woorde.
Iesus sayth she hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken from her.

funFacts: Sister of Martha; a third distinct Marie in this book alongside Marie the mother of Iesus and Marie Magdalene.

characters.name: Marie Magdalene

verses.note: Healed of euill spirits and infirmities; seuen deuils had gone out of her.
Among the women which ministred vnto him of their substance.
Comes to the tombe with spices, findes it emptie, and reports to the Apostles.

characters.perkNote: Not identified in this text with the sinfull woman of chapter 7 or with Marie of Bethany -- a traditional but text-unsupported conflation, not asserted here as fact.

spouses: unnamed reference: wife of Chuza, Herod's steward -- Luke 8:3, not individually indexed

verses.note: Wife of Chuza, Herod's steward; ministers to Iesus of her substance.
Among the women who report the emptie tombe to the Apostles.
Named among the women who ministred to Iesus of their substance.

characters.name: Marie the mother of Iames

verses.note: Named among the women at the emptie tombe who report to the Apostles.

characters.perkNote: Distinct from Marie the mother of Iesus, Marie Magdalene, and Marie of Bethany -- the fourth distinct Marie named in this book.

characters.name: Herod the Tetrarch

genealogy.father: Herod the Great -- not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: Herod being Tetrarch of Galile.
Rebuked of Iohn for Herodias his brother Philips wife; shuts Iohn vp in prison.
Hears of Iesus and is perplexed, hauing beheaded Iohn.
Warned that Herod seeks to kill Iesus; Iesus calles him 'that foxe.'
Pilate sends Iesus to Herod as a Galilean during the triall; Herod and his men of warre mocke him and send him back in a gorgeous robe; Herod and Pilate become friends that day.

characters.perkNote: Promoted to a full manager tier in this book given his expanded role across four separate scenes, including the triall scene found only in Luke (23:6-12). Distinct from Herod the Great and Herod Agrippa.

verses.note: Pontius Pilate being gouernour of Iudea.
The multitude brings Iesus to Pilate; Pilate findes no fault in him.
Declares neither he nor Herod founde Iesus worthy of death; proposes to chastise and release him.
Yeelds to the crowd's demand, releases Barabbas, and deliuers Iesus to their will.
The multitude cries out to release Barabbas, cast into prison for a certaine sedition and murther.
Pilate releases him vnto them.

characters.name: The Councel of hie Priestes and Scribes
characters.scribeTier: The Councel of hie Priestes and Scribes

verses.note: Annas and Caiaphas named the hie Priestes when the worde of God came to Iohn.
Chiefe Priests, Scribes, and the chiefe of the people seeke to destroy Iesus but feare the people.
Chiefe Priests and Scribes seeke how they might kill Iesus, fearing the people.
The Elders, chiefe Priests, and Scribes assemble, question Iesus, and leade him to Pilate.
Chiefe Priests and Scribes vehemently accuse Iesus before Herod.

funFacts: Annas and Caiaphas named together as ruling hie Priestes at 3:2, but neither individually characterized in action within this book's own text -- treated as part of the collectiue councel rather than a separate tier.

characters.name: The Ten Lepers

verses.note: Ten leprous men meete Iesus, stand afarre off, and crie, 'Iesus, Master, haue mercie on vs.'
Iesus tels them to shew themselues to the Priests; as they went, they were made cleane.
One turnes backe glorifying God and falles at Iesus feete giuing thankes -- he was a Samaritane.
Iesus askes where the other nine are, and tels the man, 'thy faith hath saued thee.'

funFacts: The text differentiates only one of the ten by description -- 'a Samaritane' -- not by name; kept as one collectiue entry rather than inventing separate identities.

characters.name: Ioseph

children: jesus_geneva_luke -- legal/adoptive father, not by blood per Luke 1:34-35

verses.note: A man whose name was Ioseph, of the house of Dauid, affianced to a virgin named Marie.
Went vp from Galile to Beth-leem, being of the house and linage of Dauid, to be taxed with Marie.
Brings Iesus to the Temple to present him to the Lord after the Lawe of Moses.
Goes to Hierusalem for the Passeouer; with Marie, seekes the twelue-yeere-old Iesus with heauie hearts.

funFacts: Iesus's genealogy in this book (3:23-38) is traced through Ioseph, called 'as men supposed the sonne of Ioseph' -- the text itself flags this as supposed descent, consistent with the virgine birth stated at 1:34-35.

characters.name: The Penitent Thiefe

verses.note: One of the two malefactors crucified with Iesus rebukes the other, and asks Iesus to remember him in his kingdome; Iesus answers, 'This day shalt thou be with me in Paradise.'

characters.perkNote: Unnamed in the biblical text; later tradition's name 'Dismas' is not asserted here as textual fact.

characters.name: Cleopas

verses.note: Two disciples walke to Emmaus discussing the crucifixion, one named Cleopas; the risen Iesus ioines them vnrecognized.
Iesus made knowen to them in the breaking of bread, then vanishes out of their sight.
They returne to Hierusalem and tell the eleuen.

characters.perkNote: Cleopas's companion is not named in the text; not assigned an identitie here.

children: unnamed daughter -- Luke 8:42, about twelue yeres of age, not individually indexed

verses.note: A ruler of the Synagogue falles at Iesus feete, beseeching him for his onely daughter, about twelue yeeres olde, lying at the point of death.
Told his daughter is dead; Iesus tels him, 'Feare not: beleeue onely, and she shalbe saued.'
Iesus raises the childe, saying, 'Maide, arise.'

characters.name: The Woman with the Issue of Blood

verses.note: A woman hauing an issue of blood twelue yeeres, healed of no physician, touches the edge of Iesus garment and is healed.
Confesses before the people; Iesus tels her, 'Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath saued thee: goe in peace.'

characters.name: The Ceturion of Capernaum

verses.note: His seruant, deare vnto him, is sicke and readie to die; the Elders of the Iewes beseech Iesus, saying he loueth the nation and built them a Synagogue.
Sends friendes saying he is not worthy that Iesus enter vnder his roofe, but to say the woorde onely, being himselfe a man set vnder authoritie.
Iesus marueiles: 'I haue not found so great faith, no not in Israel'; the seruant found whole.

characters.perkNote: Unnamed in the text; this book's spelling renders the office as 'Ceturion.'

characters.name: The Widowe of Nain

children: unnamed son -- Luke 7:12, not individually indexed

verses.note: Iesus meetes a funerall procession at Nain for her onely sonne; she is a widowe, and the Lord hath compassion, saying 'Weepe not.'
He touches the coffin, sayth 'Yong man, I say vnto thee, Arise,' and the dead man sits vp and speaks; deliuered to his mother.
Feare comes on them all; they glorifie God, saying a great Prophet is risen among them.

funFacts: Unnamed in the text; the raising of her son, unique to this Gospel, is preserved directly in this Geneva account.

characters.name: Simon the Pharise

verses.note: Desires Iesus to eate with him; when a sinfull woman washes Iesus feete with teares, he doubts within himselfe whether Iesus be a Prophet.
Iesus answers him with the parable of the two debtors, and rebukes his lacke of hospitalitie compared with the woman's loue.

characters.perkNote: Distinct from Simon Peter, Simon of Cyrene, and Simon called Zelous -- at least four men named Simon appear in this book.

characters.name: The Sinfull Woman

verses.note: A woman in the citie, which was a sinner, brings an alabaster boxe of oyntment, weeps at Iesus feete, washes them with her teares, wipes them with her haire, kisses and anoints them.
Iesus sayth her sinnes, which are many, are forgiuen, 'for she loued much'; tels her, 'thy faith hath saued thee: go in peace.'

characters.perkNote: Unnamed in the text, read directly in this Geneva account; explicitly not identified here with Marie Magdalene or Marie of Bethany, per the no-invented-identity rule.

characters.name: Simon of Cyrene

verses.note: The souldiers lay hold vpon one Simon of Cyrene, comming out of the countrey, and on him they lay the crosse to beare it after Iesus.

characters.perkNote: A fourth distinct Simon in this book, alongside Peter, the Pharise, and Zelous.

characters.name: The Sermon on the Plaine
characters.purpose: Iesus, hauing chosen the twelue, lifts vp his eyes vpon his disciples and the multitude on a plaine place, and teaches the blessed and the woes, loue of enemies, mercie, not iudging, and the parable of the wise and foolish builders (Luke 6:20-49) -- this Geneva text's own version of the sermon, shorter than Matthew's Sermon on the Mount and set on a plaine rather than a mountaine, matching the same structural distinctiveness noted in the KJV index.

verses.note: Blessed be ye poore... but wo be to you that are rich.
Loue your enemies, doe good to them which hate you, be mercifull as your Father is mercifull.
Iudge not, and ye shall not be iudged; the mote and the beame.
Euery tree knowen by his fruite; the house built on the rocke against the flood.

characters.name: The Sending of the Seuentie
characters.purpose: Iesus appoints and sends out seuentie other disciples, two and two, before his face into euery citie and place whither he himselfe would come, instructing them on provision, peace, healing the sicke, and the towns that reject them (Luke 10:1-16); they return with ioy reporting even deuils are subiect vnto them, and Iesus reioyces in spirit (10:17-24) -- content unique to this Gospel, present in the same substance here as in KJV.

verses.note: The seuentie sent forth two and two with instructions for the harvest, the labourer, and towns that receiue or reiect them.
The seuentie returne with ioy, saying euen the deuils are subiect vnto them through his name.
Iesus reioyces in spirit and thankes the Father for reuealing these things vnto babes.

characters.name: The good Samaritane
characters.purpose: In answer to a Lawyer's question, 'And who is my neighbour?', Iesus tels the parable of a certaine man fallen among theeues, passed by a Priest and a Leuite, and helped by a Samaritane (Luke 10:25-37) -- unique to this Gospel, its content confirmed present in this Geneva translation's own text of the same passage.

verses.note: A certaine man goes downe from Hierusalem to Iericho, falles among theeues; a Priest and a Leuite passe by; a Samaritane has compassion, binds his wounds, and cares for him at an ynne.
Iesus askes which was neighbour, and sayth, 'Go, and doe thou likewise.'

characters.name: Parables of the Lost
characters.purpose: To Pharises and Scribes murmuring that he receiues sinners and eateth with them, Iesus tels three parables of things lost and found: the lost sheepe, the lost groat, and the prodigall sonne (Luke 15) -- the prodigal son parable is unique to this Gospel.

verses.note: The parable of the lost sheepe, and the ioye in heauen over one sinner that repenteth.
The parable of the lost groat/peece of siluer.
The parable of the prodigall sonne, who wastes his substance and returns to his father's welcome, and his elder brother's complaint.

characters.name: Lazarus and the riche man
characters.purpose: Iesus tels the parable of a certaine riche man clothed in purple and a beggar named Lazarus laid at his gate, and their reversal of fortune after death (Luke 16:19-31) -- unique to this Gospel, the beggar being the only named figure in any of Iesus's parables in the text.

verses.note: The riche man and the beggar Lazarus; after death Lazarus is comforted in Abraham's bosome, the riche man tormented.
The riche man begs Abraham to warne his brethren; Abraham answers they have Moses and the Prophets.

funFacts: The beggar in this parable is named -- 'a certaine beggar named Lazarus' -- an unusual exception to the general pattern that Iesus's parable-figures go unnamed; not to be confused with the Lazarus of John's Gospel, a distinct figure and a distinct book.

characters.name: Parables of Prayer and Humilitie
characters.purpose: Iesus tels the parable of the vniust iudge and the widowe who continually troubles him (Luke 18:1-8) to teach that men ought alwayes to pray, and the parable of the Pharise and the Publicane praying in the Temple (18:9-14) to teach humilitie before God.

verses.note: The vniust iudge and the importunate widowe; men ought alwayes to pray, and not to waxe faint.
The Pharise and the Publicane pray in the Temple; the Publicane, who humbles himselfe, goes downe iustified rather than the other.

characters.name: The Parable of the Pieces of Money
characters.scribeTier: The Parable of the Pieces of Money
characters.purpose: As he draws neere Hierusalem, Iesus tels the parable of a certaine noble man who trauels to a farre countrey to receiue a kingdome, delivering pieces of money to his seruants to occupie till he come again (Luke 19:11-27) -- told because the people thought the kingdome of God should immediately appeare.

verses.note: A noble man delivers pieces of money to ten seruants, bidding them occupy till he come; two seruants gaine and are set ouer cities.
The seruant who hid his piece in a napkin is rebuked, and his piece taken from him and giuen to him that hath ten.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list.

luke_genealogy_3_23_38.note: Iesus's genealogy in this Geneva text runs backward from Iesus (as was supposed the sonne of Ioseph) through Heli, Dauid, Iesse, Iuda, Iacob, Isaac, Abraham, Sala, Sem, Noe, Enoch, Seth, Adam, to 'the sonne of God' -- almost entirely figures already indexed in the Genesis/Ruth/Samuel/Kings/Chronicles rosters, logged here as a bulk reference rather than re-indexed individually, matching the KJV Luke precedent. Several names between Dauid and Ioseph genuinely differ from Matthew's own genealogy (e.g. this line runs through Nathan rather than Solomon) -- a real textual divergence between the two Gospels, not resolved or 'corrected' here.
